references.text: Jebus is the old name for Jerusalem, which is also mentioned here in connection with the border of the tribe of Judah.
The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and the tribe of Judah was unable to drive them out. This explains why the city was still a foreign city at this time.
Jebus is mentioned as one of the cities in the inheritance portion of the tribe of Benjamin, showing the geographical location of the city.
David later conquered Jebus from the Jebusites and made it Jerusalem, the City of David.
Parallel account of David's conquest of Jebus, which was called Jerusalem. Shows how the city went from being a foreign Jebusite city to Israel's capital.
Lot invited the two angels to spend the night in his house, a similar hospitality situation as the servant suggests here.
